$comment: Machine-readable mirror of AGENTS/11-beta-program.md section 4. That file is
authoritative prose; this is the checkable form. `npm run beta:state` verifies
every claim here against the evidence actually on disk and fails if a phase
claims `complete` without a manifest that says `pass`.
Rule: a phase may only be `complete` if evidence.manifest resolves to a real
manifest.json whose verdict is `pass`. Anything else is `in-progress`,
`blocked`, or `not-started`. Phase 1 was once recorded complete while its
install path would have 404'd on every install; this file exists so that
cannot be asserted without an artifact behind it.
evidence.regate cites a later run against the CURRENT gate set. All three completed
phases cite the SAME run, deliberately: the gate verifies the working tree against
origin/main (21 affected projects), not one phase in isolation. Running it three
times under three labels would be theatre, not three verifications. The original
evidence.gate citation is kept because it is the historical fact of what was
actually run at sign-off.
evidence.manifest pins a SPECIFIC run for a completed phase rather than using
"latest". A completed phase was signed off on one particular capture, and "latest"
drifts with unrelated environment changes — a stale local dev server turned Phase 0
red and invalidated a claim that was never in doubt. Phases still in progress keep
"latest", because there the newest run is the point.

phases.title: adf-hx component adoption
deviations: 2026-09-23, after sign-off: the adopted breadcrumb is now upstream's inner HxpUiBreadcrumbComponent, fed the ancestors plus the current folder, rather than HxpBreadcrumbComponent, which never showed the current folder. The capture's 'links target browse-adf-hx' check had passed while every crumb but Home linked to browse-adf-hx%3Fpath%3D… — NuxeoDocumentRouterService.urlFor returned a string, and [routerLink] escapes a string's '?'. urlFor now returns a UrlTree, and the check requires the query to survive.

2026-09-23, after sign-off: the Properties and Versions tabs were REMOVED from /#/browse-adf-hx, so upstream HxpPropertiesSidebarComponent and ManageVersionsSidebarComponent are no longer rendered anywhere. Product decision: the folder tabs now match production browse (View, Permissions, History, Trash), which keeps per-document panels on the document page. The delivered entries below that say these two were adopted describe what shipped at sign-off and are left as written; the VERSION and MODEL ports and the sys pseudo-schema they drove stay and stay unit-tested. The phase-3-adf-hx evidence steps now assert the four-tab strip instead of the two panels, so the 2026-08-24 manifest is no longer reproducible for those steps.

CORRECTED: this file previously recorded that DocumentModelService "calls getModel() from its CONSTRUCTOR, so anything injecting it fails to construct". The eager call is real; the consequence was not. An async method that throws returns a rejected promise, so the service constructs. Established by writing the test rather than by reasoning about it, after the reasoning had already been written into three files.

Two evidence assertions in this phase passed while the thing they asserted was broken, because they read innerText and adf-core renders property values inside input elements. The screenshot showed Created as a raw ISO string and Creator as [object Object] while both checks reported green. Fixed by reading input values as well, and a third check added for [object Object] specifically. A negative assertion over text that does not contain the value is not an assertion.

CORRECTED: this file recorded "bridge defects: 1 of 5 verified still open". Three more are open — the dropped sort, the overwritten totalCount and the 50-child ceiling. Found by checking the code against the plan rather than against the previous entry, which is how the overstatement survived.

Phase 3 component order deviates from the plan. The plan orders metadata-sidebar and permission BEFORE manage-versions; manage-versions was taken first because metadata-sidebar was blocked on the MODEL port. permission remains unstarted, and what was adopted for metadata-sidebar is the read-only legacy properties panel, not the editable metadata sidebar — which is unadoptable (D5).

Held at in-progress until 2026-08-24 for one reason, now closed: search had never been driven against live Nuxeo. Driving it found THREE real defects, none visible to any existing check. (1) `distinctUntilChanged()` on a `Subject<void>` dropped every emission after the first, so typing a term, Next and Previous all did nothing and the page showed the unfiltered 135-document initial set while the input echoed what was typed. (2) `PACKAGED_BROWSE_COLUMNS as unknown as DataColumn[]` — `DataColumn` requires `key` and `type`, our descriptors carry `field` and `label`, so eight matching documents rendered as eight empty rows. (3) `hasNextPage` was `signal(true)` "simplified for now" AND the template never bound it, so Next stayed enabled on the last page.

The claim that the column translation was 'extracted so two consumers share it' was false when first committed: the search page used the new shared helper while the browse route kept its own copy. Corrected in a follow-up, verified by re-running the 55-check Phase 3 evidence.

Two defects in the phase-3-search evidence itself, fixed before trusting it: the paging check had a `length === 0 ||` escape that passed on zero rows — exactly the state the broken search produced — and the console-error ignore list contained 'Failed to load resource', which would have hidden any resource failure at all.

CI was RED for 16 consecutive runs (2026-08-22 to 2026-08-24) on the bundle-size step, while local gates were green and every status document said 'CI green'. The programme's own verified facts say 'Only a CI run is authoritative. A local green is necessary, not sufficient' — that rule was not followed. Root cause: CI enforces a 5 MiB ceiling on TOTAL shipped JS+CSS, set 2026-04-21 before adf-hx adoption was planned, mentioned in exactly one unrelated skill file and in no Beta document; every bundle discussion tracked the Angular *initial* budget instead. Breach began at 99db609 (document viewer, +60 kB) and was 0.60%. Ceiling raised to 6 MiB on 2026-08-24 as a recorded decision. Found by independent adversarial review, not by any gate.
notCovered: Search is now verified against live Nuxeo (phase-3-search, 13/13). Still NOT covered there: the four upstream search filter components (created-date, document-category, file-type, saved searches) remain unadopted; the HXQL translation refuses every statement it does not recognise by name; and the UI's count differs from a plain REST fulltext count because the page appends a `*` wildcard — recorded as a note, not asserted as equal.

Full viewer rendering (PDF display, zoom, pagination) is NOT verified — the evidence proves the component opens and closes, but the selected test document shows "unsupported file type". Testing pdfjs-dist rendering is adf-core's job, not ours, and the blob/rendition services are already wired.
BRIDGE DEFECTS: ALL FIVE CLOSED as of 2026-08-22. The last was hardcoded sys_effectivePermissions, now mapped from Nuxeo permissions enricher.
UPLOAD: HxPR chunked protocol vs Nuxeo batch upload are different lifecycles, not different endpoints. Bound but refusing.

MODEL write side still refuses: the Nuxeo content model is server-side configuration with no REST write path at all, so setModel, patchModel and the per-project variants are unimplementable rather than unimplemented. The READ side is implemented.
RENDITIONS getRenditions returns a fixed servable set (thumbnail, pdf); Nuxeo exposes no rendition-enumeration endpoint through this bridge, so it is not a discovery call.
QUERY getDocumentsByQuery understands ONE HXQL statement — upstream document-versions — and refuses every other by name. Adopting adf-hx search will need more.

The versions panel context menu (restore, delete, edit a version) renders but its actions are unexercised: the capture asserts the list, not the menu. Restore goes through NuxeoVersionApi.restoreVersion, which is unit-tested but has never been driven from the UI.
sysver_description is always unset: Nuxeo keeps the check-in comment in the audit log, not on the version document, so the panel never shows a version comment.

Contributor and creator columns show a Nuxeo username, not a display name. Nuxeo carries only the username on the document; a display name needs a /user/{id} lookup per distinct contributor. Open question for the team — but upstream UserService.resolveUser already caches such a lookup per id, which is a cheaper answer than first assumed.

Initial bundle 1.70 -> 3.49 MB. maximumError raised 3.5 -> 4 MB deliberately, because the properties panel left only 10 kB of headroom and the next component would have failed the build for an unrelated reason. Leadership not yet informed of either number.
The properties panel is read-only by construction ([editable]="false"), so the write path — CardViewUpdateService -> DocumentApi.updateDocument — is unexercised.

The adf-hx metadata sidebar (the newer, editable panel behind the CIC_WORKSPACE_NEW_METADATA_PANEL flag) is NOT adopted. Turning the flag on needs HxpMetadataCacheService, which has no providedIn and is not exported from the /ui barrel — neither it nor the metadata sidebar itself is.

The eager bundle has TWO causes, not one. Besides CONTEXT_MENU_ACTIONS_PROVIDERS in app.config.ts, the app shell nav drawer renders upstream HxpDocumentTreeComponent, so the shell needs adf-hx eagerly by design. Recorded as the single documented exception in the new API-surface gate; removing it means deferring the tree behind an outlet, which is Phase 4 work.

A second page has NOT been exercised in a browser: no folder on the local instance exceeds 50 children. The port paging is unit-tested (offset 100 with limit 50 becomes currentPageIndex 2) and the pager renders with an honest range, but Next has never been clicked against real data.
delivered: Secondary entry point @agentic-ui/shared/adf-hx-bridge/providers, so the app shell no longer reaches adf-hx through the bridge barrel. Measured: ports via the barrel put the initial bundle at 2.65 MB; via the entry point, 1.71 MB.

Seven of twelve API ports bound to UPSTREAM tokens with the clones deleted: DOCUMENT, QUERY, VERSION, COPY, MOVE, CHECKIN, DOWNLOAD. Six were thin over existing nuxeo-client methods; only CHECKIN needed a new one (Document.CheckIn).

AppTranslateLoader implements adf-core TranslationService five undocumented loader methods without importing adf-core, so Layer 0 manifest-labels relabelling survives and adf-core does not join the initial bundle through app.config.ts.
adf-core own i18n catalogue added to the build asset globs.

THE SWAP RUNS: upstream HxpDocumentListComponent renders on /#/browse-adf-hx over live Nuxeo — document list present, column headers matching the packaged set in order, real Nuxeo children listed, multiselect checkboxes per row. Its [schema] is fed from PACKAGED_BROWSE_COLUMNS, so Phase 2 Layer 1 drives the real adf-core DataTable.

Layer 1 field -> HxPR property translation added: DataTable reads row.obj[key], so the browse view-model keys rendered correct headers over empty rows until mapped. packaged-columns.ts had predicted exactly this.

Rehomed the three capabilities upstream does not have, then deleted the hand-written hxp-document-list: column picker (hxp-column-picker, driven by the Layer 1 descriptors, so Reset returns to the manifest rather than a packaged const), card view with thumbnails (hxp-document-cards), and the empty state. Error/retry moved to the host template earlier. Evidence: 12 of 14.

Fixed bridge defect 5 of 5 by construction: hxp-browse-columns.utils.ts wrote browse_column_settings — the SAME localStorage key production browse uses — so choosing columns on either surface overwrote the other. Those utils are deleted with the hand-written list and the POC now namespaces its own key.

ALL TWELVE API ports now bound to upstream tokens. Added USER and GROUP (over the existing UserService, mapping Nuxeo nested properties to HxPR flat User, and grouplabel->name / groupname->id), RENDITIONS (over the @rendition adapter, serving thumbnail and pdf), and UPLOAD and MODEL as refusing ports. UPLOAD and MODEL are bound rather than left unbound deliberately: eleven upstream services inject their tokens at construction, so an unbound token stops those services constructing at all, whereas a refusing port lets a component construct and fail at the point of use with a message naming the operation.

Mapping fidelity: sys_lastContributor, sys_creator and sys_lifecycleState were being dropped in favour of custom hx:* keys no adf-hx component reads, which is why the real DataTable rendered a blank Last Contributor column. All three now map to the standard HxPR fields, and date columns render via adf-core type:date rather than as raw ISO strings.
nuxeo-ui:typecheck target added and proven by reintroducing the RENDITION_API_TOKEN typo that escaped nx affected -t typecheck twice.

Breadcrumb adopted: upstream HxpBreadcrumbComponent replaces ours, which is deleted. The swap was one line; the real work was overriding adf-hx DocumentRouterService, which builds /{repository}/documents/{id} routes this app does not have and feeds them to [routerLink]. It has no providedIn, so it is an intended substitution point. NuxeoDocumentRouterService gained urlFor(options) returning a router path and urlForParent, and is bound against it. The capture asserts every crumb link targets browse-adf-hx and none targets upstream shape.

Document tree adopted: upstream HxpDocumentTreeComponent replaces hxp-browse-nav-tree in the app shell nav drawer, and ours plus HxpBrowseNavTreeService are deleted. Needed DocumentTreeDatabaseService provided (no providedIn) and the host converting a selected Document to a path for AdfHxBrowseContextService. Initial bundle cost measured at +80 kB (3.15 -> 3.23 MB), which is why it went in directly rather than behind ExtensionOutletComponent.

manage-versions adopted: upstream ManageVersionsSidebarComponent renders real Nuxeo versions in a new Versions tab. This ADDS a capability the POC never had rather than replacing one of ours, and it is the first thing to drive the VERSION and QUERY ports through the UI.

QUERY port gained getDocumentsByQuery — the free-text HXQL entry point upstream SearchService uses, which the bridge had never implemented. It recognises upstream document-versions statement whole and refuses anything else BY NAME, because an unrecognised query returning an empty result set is indistinguishable from an empty repository. It also refuses a non-empty sort rather than discarding it, which is the defect getDocumentsByNamedQuery still has.

Versions are read through Document.GetVersions, not the NXQL search. Measured on the local instance: immediately after two check-ins the NXQL/OpenSearch path returned one of two versions and both only after the index caught up, so a panel reloading on check-in would omit the version just created. getVersions (NXQL) is left alone because document-detail and the bulk-action services depend on its paginated shape.

Version mapping: Nuxeo sends NO versionLabel, so sysver_title is composed from uid:major_version and uid:minor_version; sys_parentId is overridden to versionableId because Nuxeo parentRef on a version is the live document FOLDER and upstream follows sys_parentId to reload the live document.

The Versions tab acts on the row SELECTED in View, not on the browsed folder, and says so when nothing is selected. Bound to the folder it would have looked like a working feature: upstream always prepends a current-version entry, so a folder with no versions still renders one row.

FIXED: Angular development configuration REPLACES the assets array rather than merging it, so only the base array carried adf-core translation glob and every dev server on this branch 404ed the catalogue while production shipped it. Diagnosed for a session as a stale dev server. A new review guardrail now fails when any configuration overrides assets and omits a base entry, verified by breaking it on purpose.

FIXED: adf-hx own i18n catalogues were never served. adf-hx components DO register them (provideTranslations in each component providers) but registration happens at component construction, long after the language loaded, and AppTranslateLoader.init is a no-op — so the registration landed and the strings never arrived. The versions panel rendered MANAGE_VERSIONS.DIALOG.TITLE as its heading. Both catalogues are now seeded like adf-core, and the bundle gate asserts all three ship.
FIXED: adf-hx own icon set (assets/images/*.svg) was never served, 404ing Folder.svg and Folder_open.svg on every tree render.

FIXED: NG0201 No provider found for _AsyncPipe. adf-hx UserResolverPipe calls inject(AsyncPipe) in its constructor and AsyncPipe has no providedIn, so any component rendering a user name threw WHILE rendering — the panel shell appeared with an empty body. AsyncPipe is now in the bridge provider array.

FIXED: user names rendered as "undefined undefined". Upstream UserResolverService.getFullName is `${firstName} ${lastName}` with no guard, and our mapper deliberately left both unset. The username now fills firstName with lastName empty, in both the document mapper and the USER port — which also fixes Nuxeo own Administrator, whose firstName and lastName are empty strings.

Evidence step 4 no longer screenshots an untouched list under the name row-selection: it selects a row, asserts the checkbox reports itself checked, then clears the selection. The screenshot audit had caught the two images being byte-identical.

MODEL read side implemented, so eleven of the twelve ports now do real work and only UPLOAD refuses wholesale. New ContentModelService reads /config/types, /config/facets AND /config/schemas — three calls because none is complete: /config/types omits every schema only a facet reaches (48 vs 98 on the local instance) and lists a doctype facets by name with no way to know what they contribute. Cached for the application lifetime with shareReplay refCount false, because the content model is server-side config that changes only on package install, and upstream builds its model observable in a constructor that several services subscribe to independently.

The MODEL mapping is mostly a renaming exercise and deliberately so: adf-hx FieldType values are boolean/blob/complex/date/double/long/object/string with [] variants — EXACTLY Nuxeo own type strings — and DocumentModel.resolveType passes an unrecognised type straight through, so model.types is left empty rather than populated with synthesised entries that could only change types already correct.

The one real transformation is field KEYS. HxPR keys a schema fields by their PREFIXED name (prefix dc, fields { dc_title }) because getSchemaByPrefix splits dc_title on underscore, takes dc, then requires Object.keys(fields) to contain the WHOLE dc_title. Keyed by the bare title it matches nothing and every field silently becomes FieldType.String, rendering dates as raw ISO strings. Sub-fields of a complex field stay UNPREFIXED, because getComplexFieldDetails and the dotted-path branch of getFieldDefinition both look them up by bare name. Asserted end to end through upstream own DocumentModel, not just against our mapper.

An empty Nuxeo @prefix means "use the schema name", not "no prefix": file, uid and files all report empty and Nuxeo then addresses them as file:content and uid:major_version. Read literally the keys would have been _content and _major_version.

FIXED: the document mapper emitted sys_mixinTypes SysFileish; adf-hx spells it SysFilish with no e in all four places it appears, so upstream isFile() was ALWAYS FALSE for every non-folder document we produce. Visible consequence is in PropertyUtilService.availableDocumentCategories, which feeds the metadata sidebar document-type selector: with no filish types contributed it falls back to offering only the document current type.

adf-hx-bridge can now be unit-tested against real upstream services. adf-core fesm bundle does a directory import of date-fns/locale which Node ESM resolver rejects, and Vitest externalises node_modules so resolve.alias never saw it; an alias plus server.deps.inline fixes it. That is what made the DocumentModelService integration tests possible, and they are where the field-key discovery came from.

Properties panel adopted: upstream HxpPropertiesSidebarComponent in a new Properties tab, read-only via [editable]="false" — upstream own mode rather than our scope-notice path, since suppressing the affordance is more honest than offering one that always refuses.

The document now carries TWO property surfaces, and upstream own design is what stops them duplicating: sys_* fills the panel main section via TOP_DEFAULT_PROPERTIES, and Nuxeo real properties as prefix_field fill the other section because upstream excludes sys_, sysfile_blob, sysver_ and sysgov_ from it. So a document shows its actual Nuxeo metadata — dc:nature, dc:subjects, file:content — with correct types, and nothing appears twice.

The mapper rewrites Nuxeo colon keys to underscore (dc:title -> dc_title), skips properties Nuxeo holds no value for (a properties:* read would otherwise contribute ~100 blank cards), skips unprefixed keys (they render a card with no label), and reshapes a blob from Nuxeo name/mime-type/length to the filename/mimeType/length adf-core blob card reads, dropping the download URL.

The hx:* custom keys are GONE. They duplicated Dublin Core under names no adf-hx component reads and would have rendered in the adopted panel as cards with NO LABEL, because translateProperty splits on underscore and hx:nature has none. Their four consumers read dc_* and uid_* directly now. Three browse columns that shipped hidden and rendered empty — nature, coverage, subjects — resolve as a result.

A sys pseudo-schema is added to the MODEL output, describing the fields THIS bridge emits. Nuxeo has no sys schema, so without it every sys_* field fell back to FieldType.String: Created rendered 2026-08-22T14:23:05.687Z and Creator rendered [object Object]. Caught by looking at the screenshot, not by the assertions — see corrections.

Nuxeo facets are translated to the mixins adf-hx classifies types by. SysFilish is decided by the presence of the file schema, NOT by "is not Folderish": hasMixin walks extends, Folder extends Document, and Document is not Folderish — so the fallback marked Document filish and every Folder inherited it.

Switched to upstream OWN exported provider arrays, DOCUMENT_PROVIDERS and USER_RESOLVER_PROVIDERS. AsyncPipe, UserResolverPipe, DOCUMENT_PROPERTIES_SERVICE and DOCUMENT_SERVICE had each been added in response to a separate NG0201 before the arrays turned up in provideAdfEnterpriseAdfHxContentServicesServices(). adf-core three formatting pipes stay explicit, because upstream arrays do not cover them — so that provider function alone is not enough to construct PropertyUtilService.

FIXED: sys_primaryType now carries the NUXEO DOCTYPE NAME, with SysRoot kept only for the synthetic repository root. It had been a synthetic SysFolder/SysFile, which was a mistake of ours alone: sys_primaryType is the key into Model.primaryTypes, and the MODEL port fills that with Nuxeo sixty doctypes because it is the only registry Nuxeo has. Establishing what actually depended on it showed one visible symptom and three latent ones — the properties panel Category select rendered EMPTY; extractCustomSchemaFields would find no custom schema fields for the metadata sidebar; getSubtypes silently fell back to all sixty types; and the document-category search filter emits sys_primaryType IN (...) as HXQL, which would have queried a type name Nuxeo has never heard of. So the earlier note calling it cosmetic was wrong.

The change was safe because NOTHING — upstream or ours — compares sys_primaryType against SysFolder or SysFile: folderishness travels on sys_isFolderish and sys_mixinTypes, and all four of our own readers were already written as sys_typeLabel ?? sys_primaryType, so their fallback merely stopped being wrong. isRoot() keeps working because SysRoot survives for the one node that genuinely is not a Nuxeo document.

FIXED: the POC landing screen folder header read "Repository / SysRoot", because the header renders sys_typeLabel ?? sys_primaryType and the synthetic root carried no label. Same class of defect — an internal identifier reaching a user — found in the same screenshot. Both new assertions were watched fail on purpose by reverting each fix.

docs/adf-hx-workarounds.md — the register of everything this codebase does because adf-hx or adf-core forces it, in four separated categories because they have four different audiences: 12 workarounds (6 of them STRUCTURAL, not future cleanup — the Removable column exists so a count is not misread), 6 features rehomed to the host, 4 refusing ports, 6 known-degraded behaviours.

docs/adf-hx-upstream-findings.md — adf-hx-team-facing, ordered by severity, every finding with a version, a path and a reproduction, against adf-hx 7.20.0-automate.292 and adf-core 9.0.0. Our OWN environmental problems are deliberately excluded (Node 25 localStorage, macOS lockfile pruning, Angular replacing assets arrays) because including them would weaken the credibility of the real findings.

The register is GATED, not just written: 24 markers at their sites, and a new guardrails check asserting the register and the code agree in BOTH directions plus that a marker kind matches its id category. Watched fail on purpose three ways — a 13th workaround with no row, a row whose marker was removed, and a mislabelled category. A markdown list with no gate decays the moment someone forgets a row.

Delivery record gained section 9 (open decisions awaiting a human, each with its cost of delay) and section 10 (diversions, challenges and dead ends — 12 rows, each with why it was abandoned and what it bought, including reverted work, which leaves no trace in the diff and is therefore the easiest knowledge in the repo to lose).

Process changes so it sticks: beta-phase SKILL.md step 10 now requires both new documents, states that exhaustive is the standard, and that diversions, challenges and dead ends each get their own line; and the acceptance-validator checklist gained "Is it written down?" with a verdict of incomplete if the record is thinner than the work.

FIXED the dropped sort — one of the five recorded bridge defects and the one section 3 cites as the pattern to avoid. getDocumentsByNamedQuery accepted a sort and discarded it, so no browse listing was ever ordered as intended: AdfHxDocumentService sends a default order on EVERY children fetch. HxPR sort keys are now translated to Nuxeo properties and sent as sortBy/sortOrder, which @children honours including multiple fields. Proved AT THE WIRE in evidence — a @children request carrying sortBy=dc:* — because adf-core DataTable ALSO sorts the loaded page client-side, so a reordered list alone does not prove the server was asked. That is exactly what made this defect look fixed.

A sort key Nuxeo cannot order by is now REFUSED by name rather than forwarded. Measured: sortBy=ecm:isFolder returns HTTP 200 with ZERO entries — indistinguishable from an empty folder. sys_isFolderish is therefore unmappable and the default sort dropped it; nothing regressed, because the sort was being discarded entirely, so sys_title asc is the first ordering this bridge has ever actually applied.

FIXED the overwritten totalCount. sliceQueryResult reported the page length as the total, so every caller was told the page was the whole folder. Nuxeo own number is passed through now, including its refusal to count. Established the precise rule: Nuxeo sets resultsCountLimit to the REQUESTED pageSize and counts only within it, so resultsCount is a real total exactly when the folder fits on one page and -2 otherwise — measured, pageSize=39 over 39 children answered 39 while pageSize=20 answered -2. The total is known only when there is nothing to page.

FIXED the 50-child ceiling. offset becomes Nuxeo currentPageIndex instead of slicing one oversized fetch — slicing is what made the ceiling invisible, because page two was never requested. New hxp-browse-pager (register M7), next/previous rather than numbered because a page count cannot exist when the total is only known for single-page folders. It shows a total only when the server gave one, never 1-50 of 50.

PLAN HARD RULE NOW MET: "adf-hx types must never appear in our public API signatures, enforced by a lint or API-extractor gate". New guardrails check walks each library public barrel re-export graph and fails when @alfresco/adf-hx-content-services or adf-core is reachable. It found FIVE paths on its first run, three of them genuine: BrowseAdfHxPocComponent exported from the browse barrel (so production browse carried adf-hx), AdfHxDocumentService in the bridge main barrel, and the nav drawer. Two were noise from @alfresco/adf-extensions, which leaks no type, so the gate is scoped to the two heavy packages.

Closed both fixable leaks: the POC moved to a secondary entry point @agentic-ui/feature-browse/adf-hx-poc, and isHxFolder was extracted to a dependency-free util because the router service imported it from the adf-hx-importing document service, which put @alfresco back on a barrel-reachable path.

PLAN HARD RULE NOW MET: .cursor/rules/adf-hx-browse-poc.mdc rewritten. It banned Angular Material outright — correct while every component was hand-written, wrong once five real adf-hx components were adopted and adf-core brought Material in transitively. An agent following it would have tried to remove working code. It now says prefer the real upstream component, expect Material transitively, and keep our own hxp-* components Material-free.

FIXED the last bridge defect: sys_effectivePermissions is mapped from Nuxeo permissions enricher instead of a hardcoded [Browse, Read, ReadWrite, Everything] for every document. Six permission names agree between the two vocabularies; AddChildren, RemoveChildren, Remove, Version, WriteSecurity and Unlock are translated. ManageRetention requires BOTH SetRetention and UnsetRetention, because Nuxeo splits them and holding one is not management.

An absent enricher yields UNDEFINED, not an empty array. [] asserts "this user has no permissions"; undefined says "we did not ask". Inventing either answer is how the original defect happened. upstream hasPermission treats absent as not-granted, which is conservative and correct because hiding an action is not a security control — Nuxeo server-side ACLs gate every operation.

The children fetch now requests the permissions enricher, which it previously did not request at all. Without it every row permission list would have been undefined and row-level actions would have disappeared. Asserted at the wire, on the request HEADER rather than the URL — the first version of that assertion looked at the query string and reported the enricher missing while it was being sent.

The workarounds gate learned a third state. D1 is fixed, so its marker is gone while the register keeps the row per its own rule that the history of what adf-hx cost is the point. A row marked (fixed ...) is now exempt from the must-have-a-marker check, alongside (config). The gate caught this itself — it failed the moment the marker was removed.

sys_acl implemented: NuxeoPrincipalResolver (cached directory lookups, /group/ then /user/ probe) and NuxeoAclService (async ACL builder). Nuxeo ACE names principals without saying whether user or group — verified against real ACLs where administrators and members sit beside Administrator in the same username field. The resolver also answers gap D4 (display names): a resolved user carries firstName/lastName, a resolved group carries grouplabel.

sys_acl attached to single-document reads (getDocumentById, getDocumentByPath). Children list deliberately does NOT request the acls enricher (50 ACLs for a list is expensive). Flattens Nuxeo named ACLs (local, inherited) into HxPR flat ACE[], translates permission names, uppercases status, converts null to undefined. A deleted principal is kept carrying only its name.

Evidence proved at the wire: 13 principal lookups for 4 distinct principals (ratio 3.3:1, where 2.0:1 would mean perfect caching with every principal probing group-then-user). The lookups are async and complete after properties panel renders, so the test monitors globally and checks at Health.
The /group/ 404s for users (Administrator probed as /group/, got 404, then /user/ succeeded) are now ignored by pattern — they are the expected behavior of the two-probe discriminator, not errors.

HxpUiDocumentViewerComponent adopted: opens in an overlay for the selected document, renders adf-core ViewerComponent with pdfjs-dist for PDF rendering. Preview button appears when a non-folder is selected, Escape closes the overlay. Component construction and open/close cycle verified in evidence.
Bundle impact measured: 3.49 MB → 3.55 MB (+60 KB gzipped), within acceptable range for a PDF viewer. pdfjs-dist 6.2.108 already pinned in Phase 2 workarounds.

The screenshot shows "Couldn't load preview. Unsupported file type" — that's adf-core's own ViewerComponent message, not an integration error. The component rendered correctly; the content fetch is handled by BlobDownloadService and RenditionsService which are already provided.

Permissions display: the read-only HxpBrowsePermissionsComponent is retained as the Phase 3 deliverable. It reads from Nuxeo contextParameters.acls (enricher requested in getFullDocument), displays local/inherited/external ACEs with permission names, granted-by, and time frames. The upstream PermissionsManagementPanelComponent has write capabilities through updateDocumentById which throws in Scope A, so adopting it would replace a working read-only tab with failing edits. The editable panel is deferred to GA when writes are in scope.

CORRECTION to the search claim: the search path threw on every query as shipped. The HXQL field substitution required an operator after the field name so ORDER BY was never translated, and the statement regex required WHERE which the page does not send until the user narrows something — so the first page load threw. Both fixed and pinned by wire-level specs asserting the generated NXQL. Searches now also exclude versions and trashed documents (ecm:isVersion = 0 AND ecm:isTrashed = 0), which upstream HXQL has no way to express and without which a search returned every version of every match plus the trash.
phases.verifiedOnCi: NOT verified on CI. The evidence runs need a live Nuxeo and a dev server, neither of which CI has; CI covers lint, build, test, typecheck, api-surface and fork-simulation only.

phases.title: Layer 2 — publishable platform
deviations: Merged from two duplicate entries. `phase-4-layer2` and `phase-4-platform` both carried the title "Layer 2 — publishable platform"; the latter was a stub whose notCovered read "everything". Kept the id the gate reports and the evidence directory use.

docs/phase-4-publishable-platform.md declared "Status: COMPLETE" for two commits while this file still said in-progress with no evidence cited. The prose claim preceded the artifact, which is exactly what this file exists to prevent.

The api-surface gate was materially weaker than its own commit message claimed. In a rolled-up .d.ts declarations carry no `export` prefix, so every regex missed and all 233 symbols were recorded as bare names with zero signatures — it reported `pass` while 27 published types changed. Rewritten to capture class and interface bodies; snapshot went from 420 to 2026 lines.

The platform package was built without `strictNullChecks` because libs/platform/tsconfig.lib.json extends tsconfig.base.json, which does not set `strict` — every other library sets it in its own tsconfig. 27 public types shipped wrongly non-nullable. Found by fork-simulation, not by any pre-existing gate.

The first commit after adding the api-surface gate silently corrupted its own baseline: the snapshot is a .md file, lint-staged runs prettier on *.md, and prettier rewrote quotes, indentation and long type-argument wrapping inside the fenced code blocks. Added to .prettierignore.

The generated extension library contributed a navbar entry pointing at /acme-extensions while nothing routed there, so it fell through the wildcard to /home — a nav entry that goes nowhere. The template now maps the path and ExtensionOutletComponent resolves the component by id.

ExtensionOutletComponent crashed with `Object.entries(undefined)` when used as a route component. `withComponentInputBinding()` sets every declared input from route data, passing undefined for omitted keys, which defeats the input's `{}` default. Both this template and the product bootstrap with that option, so the crash was reachable from either. Fixed and pinned by a spec that was watched failing.

B2, found by adversarial review after Phase 5 and fixed 2026-08-24: the package could not be published at all. It was compiled in Angular full compilation mode, so ng-packagr wrote a prepublishOnly script into the built package.json whose only job is to hard-fail npm publish — invalidating the phase's central claim that a customer upgrade is an npm version bump. Same root cause as the strictNullChecks deviation above: @nx/angular:package given a tsConfig REPLACES ng-packagr's bundled conf/tsconfig.ngc.json rather than layering onto it, and that file is the only place compilationMode: partial is set. Two defects from one misunderstanding. Now gated by scripts/beta-harness/publishability.mjs, which runs a real npm publish --dry-run — the only check that executes prepublishOnly — watched failing against a deliberately reverted config.

The guardrail script we tell customers to run was absent from the tarball for the whole of Phase 4, and no shipped doc mentioned it at all: the instruction existed only in the script's own header comment. Added to ng-package.json assets and documented in libs/platform/AGENTS.md §4; publishability check 5 now derives the advertised paths from the shipped docs and fails if any is missing.

docs/publish-readiness.md §4 step 5 prescribed npm publish --dry-run and was never run, because publishing was deferred — so the one procedure step that exercised this failure was the step the deferral skipped. Recorded there: a procedure step is not a check until something runs it.
notCovered: PEER INSTALLABILITY, narrowed: the `peer-installability` gate (scripts/beta-harness/peer-installability.mjs, run by `beta:gate` and by the "Verify the published package" step of .github/workflows/ci.yml) installs the built tarball from public npm with no credentials, so the nine required peers resolve at their declared ranges, and its negative control requires the same install to fail with E404 once `@hylandsoftware/satori-ui` is made required. Not covered: that optional peer itself, which only `@nuxeo-satori/platform/components-satori` imports and which needs GitHub Packages access, so nothing installs it outside this monorepo; and the template is never built from that install. The Phase 4 capture predates the gate and does not include it.

NOT PUBLISHED: `private: true` is still set and no package has ever been pushed to a registry. The scope decision is recorded in docs/publishing-to-nuxeo-registry.md (@nuxeo on packages.nuxeo.com, the registry nuxeo-elements already uses) but deliberately not executed — deferred to the final deployment stage.

The Layer 1 manifest is unexercised in the template: it ships no Nuxeo server, so `overrides` and manifest-added slots are not observed here. Phase 2 evidence covers that mechanism against the product.

The template resolves @nuxeo-satori/platform/* through workspace tsconfig aliases to source for its normal build. Only the fork-simulation gate compiles it against dist/, so the day-to-day build does not exercise a customer's resolution.

No release CI workflow, no provenance or signing, and the version (0.1.0) is hand-maintained and not tied to any release train. Whether the platform follows the Nuxeo calendar version or an independent 0.x is still an open product decision.

The api-surface gate records names, kinds and signatures only. It does not read Angular decorator metadata, so a changed component selector or input alias is invisible to it. A green run is not a promise of backwards compatibility.
@nuxeo-satori/generators has neither a test nor a typecheck target, so the generator's own code is only exercised by running it.
phases.verifiedOnCi: CI run 38158501328, completed success on Node 20, 2026-10-11: its "Verify the published package" step, which runs unconditionally, passed api-surface, publishability, peer-installability (with its E404 control), fork-simulation and upgrade-rehearsal. That verifies those gates against the package as it is now, not the Phase 4 capture, which predates peer-installability. At sign-off: NOT yet verified on CI at the time of writing. ci.yml was extended in the same change to run `typecheck`, `api-surface` and `fork-simulation` — before that it ran 5 checks against the local gate's 11, so neither new gate could protect main. The next CI run on this branch is the authoritative verification; local gates run on Node 25 with a webstorage workaround and are not authoritative.

phases.title: Layer 3 — the customer agent harness
deviations: Departed from the plan's wording deliberately, and measured first. The plan said 'split the AGENTS/ knowledge base'; 50 files carry 185 references to AGENTS/ paths, and .github/workflows/staleness-check.yml asserts AGENTS/01-services.md and AGENTS/${i}-*.md exist — so a split breaks CI and every skill. Measuring the content settled it too: 3,177 lines, of which only 3 of 13 files mention extensions, slots or the Layers. libs/platform/AGENTS.md is therefore authored for the audience, not extracted.

The plan said 'package the guardrail script'. scripts/review-guardrails.mjs is gate step 3 and checks OUR invariants — theme tokens, blob-URL lifecycles, adf-hx markers — none of which apply to a customer. A separate script with different checks ships instead; ours is byte-identical.

The three contribution generators shipped broken and reported success: every insertion was spliced inside the marker's own comment, because the indent was computed as 'everything on the line before the marker' — which is `    // `. lint, typecheck and six existing specs all passed. insertAboveMarker now asserts, after writing, that the first inserted line exists as a line of its own.

ng-packagr refuses assets from outside the package root, so the customer contract is copied into the package by a build-time sync step and gitignored, rather than committed twice. A second checked-in copy would drift, and the drift gate watches docs/, not the copy.
notCovered: THE SHIPPED GENERATOR COMMANDS ARE NOT RUNNABLE BY A CUSTOMER. libs/platform/AGENTS.md documents `nx g ./tools/satori-generators:*`, a path inside this repository. A customer who installs the package has no such path. Making the generators invocable from an installed package is unresolved and is the largest remaining gap in Phase 5.

The customer guardrail's ID-prefix check is a WARNING, not a failure: distinguishing 'registering under the platform's app. prefix' from 'referencing a platform ID to override it' needs more than a regex.
The reference-drift gate cannot tell whether a resolved slot is actually RENDERED — a component may resolve a slot and drop the result. resolve() is the closest static proxy for 'the host asks'.
No customer has used any of this. Every check is us running our own tooling against our own reference library.
phases.verifiedOnCi: Partially. CI runs api-surface and fork-simulation but NOT reference-drift or customer-guardrails, and not the evidence run. The two new gate steps have never executed on CI.

phases.title: Beta quality bar and proof
deviations: Step 0 found two defects in the coverage ratchet created by the previous day's library changes, neither of which presented as a failure: an orphaned baseline entry for the deleted drawers library, reported forever as "not measured, unchanged"; and a silent escape hatch where a project absent from the baseline was printed as new and then excluded from every check, leaving permission-dialogs at 93.85% entirely unguarded. Both now fail. --update-baseline also prunes orphans, without which the one command a maintainer would reach for could not fix the complaint.

Step 1 delivered the upgrade rehearsal. Its decisive assertion is that every slot the Layer 1 JSON manifest names still exists in the upgraded package: --break-slot toolbar leaves the compile GREEN and only that check goes red, because toolbar is named in JSON and referenced by no TypeScript. That is a clean build and a broken customer, and nothing else in the pipeline sees it.

The rehearsal compares two builds that differ only in their version string. Inventing API changes would be testing the invention, so sensitivity comes from the negative control instead. Stated in the script header rather than glossed.

Adding the 15th gate correctly turned beta:state red, because all six completed phases cited a 14/14 re-gate. Re-gated at 15/15 and re-cited rather than relaxing the check. This is the second time adding a gate has done that, and both times the gate was right.

Step 2 delivered 12 E2E specs across browse, search, document detail and the route guards. Sensitivity measured rather than assumed: with bogus credentials 9 of 12 fail, and the 3 that pass are the auth specs, which are deliberately credential-independent.

The first guard spec asserted that an unauthenticated visitor is redirected, and failed. Not a product defect: this Nuxeo has anonymous authentication enabled, so /me returns 200 as Anonymous with no credentials and the app's intentional SSO-detection path adopts that session. Recorded as a verified fact in AGENTS/11-beta-program.md section 3, because it makes a whole class of auth assertion untestable locally and will mislead the next person. Replaced with the two observable behaviours: a signed-out visitor IS redirected, and Anonymous is NOT granted administration access.

The upgrade rehearsal's check 4d, added the day before, was wrong. It ran git status and claimed to prove no edits to our sources were needed — but the script works in a staging directory and never touches the repo, so that was true by construction and unfalsifiable, while what it actually detected was uncommitted work. It turned the gate red on the commit that added the E2E project. Replaced with a real invariant: the staged customer tree must import only published entry points, checked against the upgraded package's own exports map.

That replacement check then failed to catch its own probe. A bare side-effect import has neither `from` nor parentheses, and the regex handled only from/import(/require(. The shipped customer guardrail carried the identical gap, its second cut having added the call forms and still missed this one. Both fixed and both re-probed with that exact form.

Step 3 met WCAG 2.1 AA and the baseline it was measured against was itself wrong. The phase-6-a11y capture scanned THREE surfaces and ratcheted FOUR rule ids; widening it to fifteen cases found SEVEN rule classes and 77 violating nodes, three of the classes only visible in view-mode and column-panel states a single visit per route never reaches. A ratchet over an under-sampled scan reports 'no new violations' while the ones it cannot see accumulate. KNOWN_VIOLATIONS is now empty and the verdict is unconditional.

The most widespread violation was self-inflicted and deliberate. sat-platform-nav binds ONE translated string to both matTooltip and [attr.aria-label]; our catalogues set that key to the empty string on purpose, to suppress a tooltip that duplicates the visible label. The side effect was aria-label="" on the nav toggle on EVERY surface, seven of seven, critical. An empty accessible name is invisible unless you use a screen reader, which is why it outlived every other kind of review. Reported upstream as finding 4.6: a component that uses one key for both purposes leaves the host no way to separate them.

Two accessibility fixes already in the codebase did not work. Browse carried [attr.aria-label] on its row checkboxes and axe still flagged them: Material declares aria-label as an INPUT and forwards it to the inner native control, so the attr. form lands on the host and the control stays unnamed. And the SCSS put z-index on the row's checkbox wrappers while they were position: static, where it has no effect.

The first version of the step-3 regression check was defeated, and the negative control is what proved it. It read aria-label off the live element; re-introducing the empty override turned all twelve axe assertions red and that check still reported pass, because the value it observed did not match what the earlier steps had scanned. Replaced with deterministic assertions on the three files that constitute the mechanism, each falsified individually. Fixing it also surfaced the half of the original fix that had been missed: en-fallback.ts still carried the empty strings, so a failed catalogue fetch would have silently restored the defect.

nested-interactive could not be fixed without changing behaviour, and lint enforced that. Eight clickable rows and cards were <button> elements wrapping a mat-checkbox and action buttons. The checkboxes are in-flow grid children revealed on hover, not absolute overlays, so they cannot be lifted out as siblings. The row is now a container whose title is the one control, with a stretched ::after hit area preserving row-click for mouse users. A focusable div with key handlers would reintroduce the nesting, and @angular-eslint's interactive-supports-focus and click-events-have-key-events rejected the middle ground on the first attempt.

One violation remains and it is not ours: aria-required-children, 3 nodes, @alfresco/adf-core@9.0.0 emits role="row" whose direct children are plain divs and a bare mat-checkbox. Excluded on the adf-hx step ALONE rather than in KNOWN_VIOLATIONS, so the same rule failing on a surface we own still fails the capture. Reported with the template quoted as finding 1.2, and listed second in what we most want fixed because no host can work around it without patching upstream DOM.

Scope stated rather than implied: fifteen cases over eight routes. Dialogs, the upload flow, dark mode and the pre-auth login surface are NOT covered. Login is a harness limitation - the runner sets httpCredentials, so the app authenticates before the login page can render.

The step-3 negative controls are on disk as failed manifests, not just asserted: phase-6-a11y/2026-08-24T14-37-37 (13 failures - the empty sat.* override re-introduced, every surface red), 2026-08-24T14-38-22 (the shipped catalogue blanking one key), and 2026-08-24T14-39-21 (the compiled-in fallback blanking one key). A fourth control removed the satori-ui asset glob from the 'development' configuration only and the check caught 1 of 2 asset arrays, which is the Angular replaces-rather-than-merges trap already recorded in the workarounds register. 2026-08-24T14-40-16 is the restored pass.

Step 4 added the 16th gate, supply-chain, and SAST via CodeQL. Before this the repository had NO static application security testing at all; its security assurance was `npm audit` (dependencies, not our code) plus human review - and human review is what found all nine security defects fixed after the Phase 5 adversarial review. Tooling found none of them because there was no tooling.

The SCA gate deliberately gates on `npm audit --omit=dev`, not the full audit. Dev-inclusive is 9 high and 13 moderate, none of which reaches a customer; gating on that total would be permanently red and therefore bypassed, the same reasoning as the coverage ratchet. The dev total is REPORTED on every run so it cannot be quietly forgotten either.

Accepting a finding now expires. The one production advisory (quill, low, XSS via HTML export) is allowlisted with a reason and an `expires` date, and an expired entry FAILS. An allowlist entry for an advisory the audit no longer reports also fails, because a standing acceptance of a fixed problem reads as coverage it does not provide. Six negative controls, all confirmed red: expired entry, missing entry, an unused dependency reappearing, an exception for an undeclared package, an acceptance of a non-existent advisory, and a blocking severity that the allowlist must not excuse.

The gate's fourth check found TWO MORE unused production dependencies than were recorded as debt. `openai` and `express` were known; `cors` and `dotenv` were not. All four are removed. This is not tidiness: `openai` in `dependencies` is the clearest single reason a reader concludes this application makes direct LLM calls, which it does not.

Removing them exposed the lockfile hazard from the other direction. `npm install --package-lock-only` pruned two unrelated nested @emnapi entries and the lockfile gate caught it immediately - 2 unresolvable edges. Restored the known-good lock and removed only the three root entries by hand, per the repo rule. All 225 platform-tagged entries preserved and `npm ci --dry-run` clean.

Two bugs in my own gate, both self-inflicted and both instructive. It read package.json when scanning for references, so every dependency matched its own declaration and the check found nothing. Then, with substring matching, `tslib` counted as referenced because THIS GATE'S OWN DOC COMMENT contains the string `"tslib": "^2.8.1"` while explaining the first bug. Now matched as real module specifiers only, including the bare side-effect `import 'x';` form whose omission has been a defect twice before in this repo.

A new guardrail, checkSanitizerPairing, enforces that every `bypassSecurityTrustHtml` has a DOMPurify.sanitize() or escapeHtml() in the same class member. All nine calls were already safe, but that safety is a PAIRING and nothing enforced it: deleting one sanitize() call would leave a compiling, passing, stored-XSS hole on a path that renders `note:note`, which any user with write access can author. It also underwrites the quill allowlist entry, whose stated reason is exactly that every render path sanitises. Falsified three ways including a vacuous-pass control.

Adding the 16th gate turned beta:state red again, because all six completed phases cited a 15/15 re-gate. Re-gated at 16/16 and re-cited rather than relaxing the check. This is the THIRD time adding a gate has done that, and all three times the gate was right.

CORRECTION to the step 4 entries above: SAST was NOT absent. GitHub CodeQL default setup was configured on 2026-07-24 and had analysed every push since - 87 JS/TS rules, weekly plus on-push - and was reporting 21 open alerts, 6 of them high. Every document in the repository said 'No SAST', and I repeated that claim before checking the Security tab. The gap was never the tool: a tool ran, found things, and no process consumed the output.

Two compounding reasons the alerts were invisible. Default setup analyses the PULL-REQUEST ref, so they live under refs/pull/145/head; GET /code-scanning/alerts with no `ref` reports on the default branch, where there are none, so the obvious query returned a reassuring zero - I made that exact mistake first. And nothing in the gate pipeline, the phase evidence or CI ever asked.

The advanced CodeQL workflow I added could not run at all: 'CodeQL analyses from advanced configurations cannot be processed when the default setup is enabled'. Default setup is a repository-level setting, so it was removed rather than switching that off unilaterally. Its `security-and-quality` suite would add queries over the `default` suite in use; raising the suite is a repo setting and is recorded as a decision for whoever owns it.

All 21 alerts are in scripts and tooling, not the shipped application, and all 21 are fixed. Fourteen came from ONE function: `esc()` in publish-confluence.mjs escaped & < > but not the double quote, and its output goes into double-quoted XML attributes, so a page title containing a quote closes the attribute and injects markup. Also fixed: CQL injection in findByTitle (escaped the quote but not the backslash), the same missing characters in tools/video/deck.html, regex injection from --break-slot in upgrade-rehearsal.mjs, three incomplete regex escapes in extension-reference-drift.mjs, a single-pass tag stripper in verify-confluence.mjs, and a missing permissions block in ci.yml - the only one of nine workflows without one.

Two of those were in GATES. An unescaped `$` or `(` makes a pattern match something other than the token it names, and a gate that matches the wrong thing is worse than one that fails. The upgrade rehearsal's negative control was re-verified afterwards: --break-slot toolbar still goes red on exactly one check.

The durable fix is the 17th gate, code-scanning, which reads the alerts. Its most important assertion is that a ref with no analyses is NOT a clean ref - the precise trap above, where 0 open alerts from an unscanned ref is indistinguishable from clean. Falsified four ways: an unanalysed ref via --ref, an acceptance matching no open alert, the explicit skip printing NOT RUN rather than pass, and the blocking-severity path, which was observed failing on all 6 real highs before they were fixed rather than on a synthetic case.

Stated limitation, not papered over: alerts are keyed to a ref and CodeQL runs in parallel with CI, so the newest analysis can predate HEAD. The gate prints the analysis timestamp for that reason, and it is deliberately NOT in CI - on a fresh push it would fail on the previous commit's alerts, including ones the push fixes, and a gate that goes red for work already done is one people learn to ignore. It runs in the phase gate. Wiring it into CI means waiting on the CodeQL check first, which is a deliberate CI change rather than a side effect of this step.
Adding the 17th gate turned beta:state red for the fourth time. Re-gated at 17/17 and re-cited.
notCovered: A phase-6 evidence manifest covering the whole phase. phase-6-a11y covers accessibility alone, which is why this phase is still `in-progress`. Its count here read 12/12; the cited manifest 2026-08-24T14-40-16 records totals {steps:13, checks:27, failed:0}, so 27/27 is the figure and docs/beta-delivery-record.md had it right. AND IT IS NO LONGER PASSING: every capture from 2026-09-15T00-32-51 to 2026-09-16T08-51-23 reports failed:3 — button-name, axe serious/critical, on browse, browse cards and the browse column panel. That puts step 3 (WCAG 2.1 AA) back in question, undiagnosed as of 2026-09-23. Step 6 is reopened because shared-ai-client is in scope at 15.98%. That makes the step count 5 of 7, not 6. Step 5 is NOT open; see the Safari/WebKit entry below, whose earlier text wrongly implied it had never run.

Unit coverage: 10 of 11 in-scope projects clear 90% as of 2026-09-22 — shared-ai-client is in scope at 15.98%, so step 6 is REOPENED. It reads 10 of 10 only if the AI client is excluded, which the plan's scope contract does not do. Separately, 6,137 in-scope lines across 34 files are EXCLUDED from the denominator and unscheduled (10,155 lines across 48 files in total, counted as newlines, re-measured 2026-09-22). The percentage is real for what it measures and says nothing about those. Out of Beta scope and not held to the bar, measured 2026-09-22: acme-extensions 53.47%, administration 60.39%, knowledge-discovery 65.03%, tasks 43.2%, assets 97.44%. The assets figure is not evidence of anything — it comes from 78 measured statements while 1,644 lines of its two components are excluded from the denominator.
note-editor.ts sits at 75.7%: four Quill-DOM methods need a live editor instance rather than a mock. The library clears 90% overall regardless.

Safari/WebKit: a `webkit` project IS registered in apps/nuxeo-ui-e2e/playwright.config.ts alongside `chromium`, and that file states the rule that it is registered only once the suite passed on it — so this entry's previous text, "never run... registers no webkit project", was false rather than merely stale. What remains true: WebKit is not Safari. It shares Safari's engine but not its UI, its extensions, or iOS's stricter storage rules, and no real Safari or iOS device has been tested.

The E2E suite does NOT run in PR CI. It needs a Nuxeo container with OpenSearch plus a served app, and verify-gate has no precondition-not-met path, so it is a phase gate run against the local stack. A check that only runs when someone remembers is a real limitation, not a solved problem.
The platform has never been published to a registry, and no test resolves its peer dependencies from a clean install. The first real publish is to be tagged alpha for exactly that reason.

The adopted upstream permissions panel represents 3 of Nuxeo's 12 permission levels. Documents holding any other now have their ACL write REFUSED rather than silently stripped — including, on a stock instance, the `sections` root and any Comments container. Correct behaviour, but the panel cannot edit those documents at all.
